answer: An agent economy can anchor reputation in a grove of long-lived, stake-backed identities: each agent posts a bond tied to one verified identity, and its standing grows only through attested work over time. A new identity starts with zero trust, so a Sybil attacker spinning up thousands of sock-puppets faces a spiral of costs — each fake must fund its own bond and slowly earn history before it can influence anything, making large-scale fakery expensive while honest agents keep their earned standing.
